## Claims
### claim-000
evidenceId: live-web-0

In 2010, Japan had a labor force of 65.9 million people, representing 59.6% of the aged 15 years and older. Japan employment and mobility have structural characteristics that affect how quickly a career switch can happen. Affects whether timing favors acting now versus deferring.
### claim-001
evidenceId: live-web-1

Foreign workers in Japan — reference for decision research. Japan employment and mobility have structural characteristics that affect how quickly a career switch can happen. Affects feasibility of execution in the local context.

evidenceId: live-github-0

### claim-003
evidenceId: live-github-1

This is a project on the effects of COVID-19 on labor markets in Japan. Labor-market signals suggest skill and demand alignment should be validated before committing. Affects whether timing favors acting now versus deferring.
### claim-004
evidenceId: live-github-2

Time-series forecasting in labor, goods and services, and financial markets of Japan using ARIMA methods. Labor-market signals suggest skill and demand alignment should be validated before committing. Affects whether timing favors acting now versus deferring.
### claim-005
evidenceId: live-github-3

A mobile-first web app that helps foreign workers, international students, and professionals in Japan find the perfect Japanese business phrase for any situation. Labor-market signals suggest skill and demand alignment should be validated before committing. Affects feasibility of
### claim-006
evidenceId: live-github-4

NLTK-based NLP analysis of sentiment/themes in Japan's Specified Skilled Worker Program discussions. Labor-market signals suggest skill and demand alignment should be validated before committing. Affects whether timing favors acting now versus deferring.
### claim-007
evidenceId: live-github-5

AI exposure analysis of Japanese job market (~556 occupations). Labor-market signals suggest skill and demand alignment should be validated before committing. Affects whether timing favors acting now versus deferring.

## Options (human chooses — no automatic recommendation)
### opt-change-career: Change career path now (staged transition)
supporting_evidence: live-web-0, live-web-1, live-github-0, live-github-1, live-github-2, live-github-3, live-github-4, live-github-5
advantages: Supporting signal: In 2010, Japan had a labor force of 65.9 million people, representing 59.6% of the aged 15 years and older. Japan employment and mobility ha; Can start with a staged move rather than an all-or-nothing jump; May improve long-term optionality if demand signals hold
risks: Income discontinuity during transition; Market timing or hiring-cycle mismatch; Skills gap versus target role requirements
unknowns: Target role compensation range in Japan for your profile; How portable current skills are to the destination path; Personal runway and household constraints
### opt-stay-or-defer: Stay / defer change and gather stronger evidence first
supporting_evidence: live-web-0, live-web-1, live-github-0, live-github-1, live-github-2, live-github-3, live-github-4, live-github-5
advantages: Preserves current income stability while researching; Allows targeted upskilling before committing; Can validate weak spots such as: Foreign workers in Japan — reference for decision research. Japan employment and mobility have structural characteristic
risks: Opportunity cost if the window for switching narrows; Staying too long in a declining fit
unknowns: How long to defer before a hard go/no-go date; Whether internal mobility is a better bridge than an external switch
